ggm_message.why: The Language Subtag Reviewer explaining, in 2014, why one code was never added.

iso639_3_retirements.why: The upstream registration authority's own list of every code element it has retired.

rfc1766.why: 1995. Names the editions of ISO 639 and ISO 3166 that fix the registry's memory floor.

rfc3066.why: 2001. The tag registry the subtag registry was built out of.

rfc4645.why: 2006. Initialisation rules, and a memo whose own contents were removed before publication.

rfc4646.why: 2006. The promise: withdrawn codes remain valid in language tags.

rfc5645.why: 2009. The bulk import of ISO 639-3, and the sentence that sets the second memory floor.

rfc5646.why: 2009. The promise restated, plus the note on records deprecated before they were added.

subtag_registry.why: The registry itself. Every subtag ever assigned, with Added and Deprecated dates.

note: Feeds, not copies. The registry and the RFCs stay in the gitignored cache; sources/ keeps the decisive records cut out of them by evidence.py, plus the SHA-256 of every whole file, so any claim here can be checked against the original at its published URL.
